text: What is inverted in "inversion of control"?
choices: The component tree is built from the leaves upward rather than from the window down.
Your code no longer calls the toolkit in an order you wrote; the toolkit calls your handlers when things happen.
Events are delivered in reverse order of registration, so the last listener runs first.
The model depends on the view rather than the other way round.
explanation: After the interface is built, `main` does nothing until the program exits, and all behavior lives in handlers called from outside in an order nobody wrote down. Section 22.1.2's template method was a small version of the same idea — a parent calling into a subclass's steps — and this is it governing a whole program. Three things follow: there is no single flow to read, state becomes the connection between handlers, and no handler may assume another has run.
